questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A place close to home, with a warmer climate, interesting culture and delicious food.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Really difficualt. I was very stressed out in the begining and felt very left alone with no other from my study and no one at University of Milan. It was hard to manage your own scheduale and choose your own courses. But dont stress about it! It all worked out and the italians are very chill with deadlines and so on. Also if courses overlap, that is no problem. In italy it is very common to take non attending courses.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Not much. Your should go to the school and get a stamp on your certificate to confirm that you arrrived.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was really hard. My advice is to go searching early. It gets harder the close to moving you get.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived with an elderly couple, who i had a connection to through a freind of mine. I would reccomend staying with some old people. It is much cheaper and a fantastic cultural experience.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had a meeting with my contact person called massimo. I was very confused and he was a bit frustrated with me. I ended up writing to the KU facebook group, and received a lot of help, and took a lot of interesting courses with a lot of nice danish people.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not a lot. Only massimo

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: It worked well

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use eachother. Write to the other exchange students and join the ku group.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was very interesting topics, but a lot different from danish school.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I am a bachelor student but i took masters courses. It was a good level. Not too hard, not too easy.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different. More in class presentations as a part of your grade, and also a lot less structured.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Digital socielty
Journalism, media and politics
Anthropology of AI
Corporate communication

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Digital society! A very talented teacher from USA. He speaks english that is easy to understand. I found it a bit difficult to understand the italian teachers.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I traveled a lot around in italy, and the train tickets can be quite expensive.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: food and drinks were very cheap if you come the right places. Train tickets were more expensive than i thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I dont know if there were any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: i dont know

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Go watch football games and basketball! Such a fun experience. Also go to villa necchi and all the nice attractions.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go on trips to citys close by. Bergamo is wonderfull, also Parma, Bologna, verona and so on.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: You need to be patient. Italiens are very layed back and take their time.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Hang out after school.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The aspect of time. In Denmark we are very particular with times, but in italy they are very loose.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The loving and welcoming culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Save up some money and try to get some scholarships. It is expensive to be abroad, you forget that you are not on vacation all of the time. Also, back less luggage than you think! There are so many nice things to buy in Milan.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Fitnesses are expremely pricey. But running is nice! There are just not a lot of parks. Also! the taxa system is so bad. The metro stop after 00 at night, and it is very difficault to find a taxi.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the amazing freindships i got.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: To be on my own, without a community to help me.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Milan is amazing

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
